look_here_first: Once you know it is an ash, go to the lower leaflet surface and the samara: Texas ash usually has a glaucous white-reticulate waxy underside, a relatively small seed body, and a wing that is terminal or only slightly decurrent.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: opposite branches and odd-pinnate leaves, usually 5–7 leaflets

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: lower leaflet surface characteristically glaucous with white-reticulate wax

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaf scar depressed-obovate with shallowly concave/notched upper margin

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: samara body small, with wing terminal or only slightly decurrent

key_traits.label: Leaf morphology
key_traits.text: Usually 5–7 relatively short/broad leaflets; margins entire to distally crenulate/serrate.

key_traits.label: Abaxial surface
key_traits.text: Glaucous, often with dense white-reticulate wax overlay.

key_traits.label: Leaf scar
key_traits.text: Depressed-obovate, shallowly concave/notched above, sides somewhat flaring.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Samara body about 1 cm; wing terminal or only slightly down distal quarter.

key_traits.label: Bark
key_traits.text: Gray, becoming furrowed with interlocking flattened ridges.
